title: Installment Payment Plans Renewal Bill
content:
**Rule.** The renewal bill of the **Installment Payment Plans** is issued with the renewal offer on the renewal term's own plan. Its premium portion is the renewal full-term premium multiplied by the plan's renewal down payment percentage and divided by 100, rounded to the cent; its fees are the renewal policy fee and any filing fee due; and it is due on the expiration date of the expiring term. Only one renewal bill is issued per renewal term (the plan's existing renewal bill is the evidence). On plans whose renewal down payment is drafted automatically (the Cardinal Point Monthly EFT Plan and the Cardinal Point Monthly Card Autopay Plan) the renewal down payment is drafted on the due date under the recurring authorization.

**Worked example (hypothetical).** A renewal term on the Cardinal Point Monthly EFT Plan with a renewal full-term premium of 1,250.00, a renewal policy fee of 20.00 and no filing fee due: the premium portion is 16.6 percent of 1,250.00, which is 207.50; the renewal bill is 207.50 plus 20.00, which is 227.50, due on the expiration date of the expiring term and drafted on that date. On the Cardinal Point Six-Pay Direct Bill Plan the same renewal would carry a premium portion of 16 percent, 200.00, and would not be drafted.
